title: Slot smoothing, decay, and tenant reintegration — PRD (wip)
content:
Purpose:
This doc sketches a feature set for smoothing short-term slot allocations ("micro-bursts"), decaying ephemeral credits gracefully, and reintegrating tenants back into normal tenancy after preemptions or soft-evictions. The goal is to reduce noisy-neighbor impact during bursts while avoiding long tail capacity churn and surprising tenant behavior.

Problem statement / Why this matters:
- Today tenants can grab short-lived surge capacity which produces sharp latency spikes and makes isolation boundaries brittle.
- When we preempt or throttle tenants aggressively we often leave them in a degraded state that requires manual intervention or long cooldowns, increasing support load.
- Existing burst credit systems either (a) refund too slowly and waste capacity, or (b) evict tenants too harshly and cause oscillation.
- Product teams need predictable degradation curves and an automated reintegration path so applications recover smoothly.

Success metrics (initial):
- Reduce tenant-triggered 95th percentile latency variance across pools by 20% in surge windows.
- Reduce manual tickets related to post-eviction recovery by 50% in Q2 after rollout.
- Keep burst credit carryover (unused) below 5% of daily pool capacity.

Non-goals:
- Replace full dedicated autoscaler. This complements, not supplants, predictive prewarm/autoscale.
- Solve long-term capacity forecasting. Focused on short-term smoothing and behavioral controls.

High-level design:
1) Slot smoothing controller (SSC):
   - Maintain a short-timescale moving-capacity window per tenant (e.g., 30s–5m) that limits the rate of slot expansion and contraction.
   - Instead of instant grant/deny for a slot request, SSC answers with a soft-accept confidence (0..1). Requests above threshold enter a fast-path; others are queued with bounded latency.
   - Interface: internal RPC between routing and capacity broker; minimal API change (accept_rate_hint).

2) Decay policy for burst credits:
   - Burst credits have two axes: amplitude (how much capacity granted) and half-life (how quickly credit decays back into baseline).
   - Policy templates: "fast-decay" (aggressive return to baseline; half-life 2m), "balanced", "sticky" (half-life 15m). Admins/tenants choose per-commitment.
   - Credits reduce gradually to avoid sharp eviction spikes. Decay is time-based and shapeable (exponential vs linear).

3) Tenant reintegration workflow:
   - State machine: NORMAL -> SOFT_DEGRADED -> PREEMPTED -> PROBATION -> NORMAL.
   - On preemption, tenant is placed in PROBATION with controlled ramp-up: we re-introduce slots at small increments and verify key SLO signals (latency, error rate, KV cache warmness).
   - Violations during PROBATION cause fallback to SOFT_DEGRADED with longer cooldown.

4) Isolation controls and heuristics:
   - Short-circuit for critical tenants (admin opt-outs) to bypass smoothing for emergency bursts.
   - Feature flags to toggle per-pool enforcement.
   - Multi-tenant fairness mode: when multiple tenants burst, scoring function favors tenants with better historical efficiency (tokens-per-inference latency) to reduce cost blowups.

5) Console + API UX changes:
   - New console panel: "Burst health" showing real-time smoothing window, decay curve, and probation states per tenant.
   - API: new optional params on capacity reservation calls: "burst_profile":string, "probation_checkpoints":comma-separated metrics.

Operational considerations:
- Telemetry: expose per-tenant smoothing window metrics (window_size_s, current_granted_slots, decay_rate), probation transitions, and soft-accept counts.
- Alerts: create a SLO for reintegration failure rate > 10% / day.
- Runbooks: automated remediation to extend probation, or temporarily increase half-life if repeated oscillation detected.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Canary (internal + 3 low-risk customers) — enable SSC in conservative mode (fast-decay) for 2 weeks. Monitor telemetry and tickets.
2) Beta (select paying dedicated customers) — add console UI and allow choosing profiles; gather UX feedback.
3) Gradual opt-in with default off for all tenants, then default-on for new tenants after stable telemetry (6–8 weeks).

Backward compatibility and safety nets:
- Default behavior for existing tenants is unchanged until they opt in.
- An escape hatch API to forcibly revert a tenant to legacy burst behavior.
- Safe-mode: if controller detects degraded cross-pool SLOs it auto-rolls back.

APIs & Data model (sketch):
- POST /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/burst_profile {"profile":"balanced","requested_slots":12}
- GET /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/probation_status -> {state, allowed_slots, cooldown_until}
(backend shape to be iterated; API team to review for backwards-compat.)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How to tune decay half-lives for different hardware classes (A100 vs L40): function of per-token latency? Ops input needed.
- Scoring fairness vs contractual priority (how to respect committed reservations while still penalizing inefficient usage).
- UX: should probation be visible to tenant or only operator? Early preference: visible but gated (opt-in messaging).
- Cost accounting: how to bill for slots during probation—full price or discounted? CFO input required.

Risks:
- Mis-tuned decay could increase average latency if we hold too much headroom for too long.
- Complexity of state machine increases surface area for bugs and observability debt.
- Customer confusion if reintegration semantics are not documented clearly; may increase support volume temporarily.

Open TODOs:
- [ ] Simulation: build a synthetic load simulator that exercises smoothing windows and compares to baseline autoscaler (SRE + Applied ML).
- [ ] Concrete API spec and backward-compat test matrix (API + SDK teams).
- [ ] Billing recommendation from finance for probation window usage.
- [ ] Implementation spike: SSC prototype in the broker (2-week spike).
- [ ] Design console mockups for burst health panel (design + product).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally focused on short-timescale behavior and tenant recovery. If Reviewer prefers a deeper integration with predictive warm-pools, call that out and we can merge designs.
- Comments inline OK; I expect several rounds of iteration on fairness scoring and half-life defaults.

References and related docs:
- See: shared_drives/product/dedicated/ephemeral-surge-negotiator-and-fair-share-prd-notes.json (related thinking; this doc tries a softer, decay-first approach).
- Jira: RDW-2107 (proto), RDW-2186 (console), RDW-2220 (billing).

Next steps (2-week cadence):
- Week 1: alignment meeting with SRE + Applied ML + Billing (owners: Priya/Ethan).
- Week 2: small prototype + simulation results and initial canary invite list.

Author: Priya Rao (product)
